definitions.explanation: The month after this one; the coming month. Used to refer to future events or plans in the month that follows the current one.

examples.english: What will you do next month?
I'm going to Japan next month. I'm very happy about it.
My friend is coming from Japan at the beginning of next month, so I'm really looking forward to it.
I'll start working at a new company next month. I'm busy preparing now, but I'm looking forward to it.

notes:
{来月|らいげつ} refers to the month following the current one and can function as both a noun and time adverb.

TIME REFERENCE SERIES:
- ⟦{先月|せんげつ}→せんげつ：00751⟧: last month
- ⟦{今月|こんげつ}→こんげつ：00720⟧: this month
- {来月|らいげつ}: next month

The {来|らい} prefix means 'coming' or 'next' and appears in ⟦{来週|らいしゅう}→らいしゅう：00746⟧ (next week) and ⟦{来年|らいねん}→らいねん：00745⟧ (next year).

USAGE:
Like other time nouns, {来月|らいげつ} often appears without a particle: {来月|らいげつ}⟦{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}します→ひっこす：01171⟧ (I'm moving next month). Use の to connect to nouns: {来月|らいげつ}の⟦{予定|よてい}→よてい：00824⟧ (next month's plans).
